topic: Exact fixed-bin recovery of acyclic Hawkes graphs from two covariance lags. For a stationary labeled multivariate linear Hawkes process with known bin width Delta, positive baselines, a common unknown exponential decay, nonnegative zero-diagonal acyclic excitation matrix, and at least one edge, prove that the mean plus Gamma_1 and Gamma_2 identify beta, every edge amplitude, and the baselines. Establish Gamma_k=exp((A-beta I)(k-1)Delta)J^2K, im Gamma_1=im A, recovery of beta from the restricted transition, exact finite nilpotent-log deconvolution, and edge recovery from the antisymmetric covariance jump. Cover singular A, repeated poles, disconnected components, and zero-edge nonidentification; derive rank-adaptive consistent estimation, support recovery, and simultaneous graph confidence sets. Consumer: Qiao et al.'s metropolitan cellular-alarm logs recorded at 1–9 second resolution. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolver derived K=A(2 beta I-A)Q with Q positive definite and A_ij=max(K_ij-K_ji,0)/lambda_j; a covariance-only Gamma_0,Gamma_1,Gamma_2 corollary also emerged. Recovery passed 400 random/adversarial DAGs (p=2–9, worst error 8.31e-10), 24 independent bin-integral checks, and 207 three-node alias searches. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Complete a basis-invariant HAC/rank-truncation delta-method proof with explicit conditioning margins and independently audit the two-lag algebra. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce diamond and proportional-row cases by independent quadrature; any legal violation of im Gamma_1=im A or the recovered covariance limit kills the theorem.

open_problems.open_problem: Does the stationary mean together with exactly two positive-lag bin-count covariance matrices identify the common exponential decay, every directed excitation amplitude, and every baseline for every nonzero labeled acyclic Hawkes graph, including singular, disconnected, and repeated-pole cases?

source_refs.claim: Exponential multivariate Hawkes graphs are recovered from second-order moments by locating decay modes in the full covariance spectrum and evaluating transforms of the covariance density, not from two fixed-bin lags.
source_refs.author: Jalal Etesami, Kun Zhang, Kushagra Singhal, and Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: The full continuous-time first- and second-order statistics uniquely characterize a stationary multivariate Hawkes kernel through a Wiener–Hopf equation, but no finite-bin two-lag sufficient statistic is given.
source_refs.author: Emmanuel Bacry and Jean-François Muzy

source_refs.claim: Multivariate fixed-bin Hawkes inference is handled by latent-time MC-EM; the paper does not derive a two-covariance-lag identifying map.
source_refs.author: Leigh Shlomovich, Edward A. K. Cohen, and Niall Adams

source_refs.claim: Low-resolution event sequences create instantaneous-effect identifiability failures for ordinary discrete Hawkes Granger-causality methods, motivating a separate structural model.
source_refs.author: Jie Qiao, Ruichu Cai, Siyu Wu, Yu Xiang, Keli Zhang, and Zhifeng Hao

source_refs.excerpt: characterize when transition-probability data identify the sign or zero of a disease/death component interaction

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature proves uniqueness from an entire covariance-density function, searches decay modes in a full covariance spectrum, or estimates binned models by Whittle, INAR approximation, or latent-time likelihood. The prior semigroup proposal separately identified partially observed recovery of an unknown generator as the nonroutine direction. No located source supplies an exact inverse from only the mean and two fixed-bin covariance lags. The concrete obstruction is rank loss: for singular A the ambient ratio Gamma_2 Gamma_1^{-1} does not exist, so the transition must be defined basis-invariantly on an observable image; repeated poles and disconnected components also rule out eigenvector-by-eigenvector arguments, and direction must still be separated from a symmetric covariance contribution.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit basis-invariant map from (lambda, Gamma_1, Gamma_2, Delta) to (beta, A, mu), with a proof of injectivity for every nonzero acyclic model and a complete zero-edge observational-equivalence statement.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames coarse time resolution as a structural-identification problem rather than merely an estimation inconvenience.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: coarse event timestamps create apparent simultaneity -> ordinary Hawkes Granger ordering loses within-bin direction -> exploit explicit process structure to recover the causal graph exactly

method_exemplars.technique: Derive the covariance-to-kernel Wiener–Hopf relation and prove uniqueness of its causal solution.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the canonical second-order Hawkes identification result; the desired resolution would compress its infinite-dimensional covariance input to two matrices by exploiting exponential dynamics and acyclic nilpotence.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove mixing for bin counts and use a score/Hessian expansion to obtain consistency and asymptotic normality of a second-order estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies rigorous limit theory under genuine fixed-bin Hawkes observation, the same sampling regime in which the finite-lag recovery map must be estimated.

open_problems.open_problem: Can empirical Gamma_1 and Gamma_2 support basis-invariant, rank-adaptive estimation, exact graph support recovery, and simultaneous edge confidence sets when rank(A) is unknown and singular values may approach the truncation boundary?

source_refs.claim: Whittle estimation from Hawkes count data is consistent and asymptotically normal under mixing and moment conditions, but it does not treat multivariate rank selection or graph-wide inference.
source_refs.author: Felix Cheysson and Gabriel Lang

source_refs.claim: High-dimensional Hawkes network tests use continuous-time integrated-history regressors and martingale limit theory, not a data-dependent image projection of fixed-bin covariance lags.
source_refs.author: Xu Wang, Mladen Kolar, and Ali Shojaie
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Nonasymptotic confidence polyhedra for Hawkes network weights are obtained from continuous-time likelihood-score martingales, assuming exact event-time observation rather than fixed-bin covariance inversion.
source_refs.author: Haoyun Wang, Liyan Xie, Alex Cuozzo, Simon Mak, and Yao Xie

source_refs.excerpt: Fully data-measurable selection of the dominating geometry and simultaneous lag inference is also open.
operator-norm contraction ... uniformly on classes bounded away from zero affine separation

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two-lag recovery map is nonsmooth where rank(Gamma_1) changes and ill-conditioned when its smallest nonzero singular value, the restricted-transition separation, or an edge amplitude approaches zero. The in-repo Hankel and BACKSHIFT results supply rank-stratified pseudoinverse and conditioning-margin templates, but their first proof steps do not cover temporally dependent Hawkes bin counts, a random range basis, or differentiation of a restricted matrix logarithm. Existing binned Hawkes asymptotics avoid an estimated image subspace, while existing Hawkes confidence sets use exact event-time likelihood scores. A valid result must therefore combine a joint HAC CLT for mean and lag covariances with spectral-projector perturbation, rank selection, logarithm differentiation, and max-norm simultaneous calibration.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A total rank-selection estimator with explicit singular-value, decay, stability, and edge-strength margins, a basis-invariant asymptotic linear representation for (beta_hat, A_hat, mu_hat), and a HAC or multiplier procedure giving graph-wide coverage and beta-min support recovery.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates Hawkes network recovery through honest edge-level uncertainty rather than point-estimation accuracy alone.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Hawkes weights encode directed links -> estimated links are scientifically unreliable without uncertainty quantification -> construct simultaneous graph statements with guaranteed coverage

method_exemplars.technique: Establish mixing of fixed-bin counts, a CLT for second-order empirical functionals, and delta-method limit theory for Hawkes parameters.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest rigorous asymptotic theory under the same fixed-bin Hawkes observation regime.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine high-dimensional Gaussian approximation, long-run covariance estimation, and multiplier bootstrap for simultaneous inference under temporal dependence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired graph set is calibrated from a maximum over many nonlinear transforms of dependent lag-covariance averages.

method_exemplars.technique: Use basis-free spectral-projector perturbation expansions with explicit spectral-gap dependence to derive concentration and asymptotic normality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The first nonstandard step is estimating im(Gamma_1) stably and invariantly when the target matrix is rank deficient.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the stationary intensity vector and Hawkes baselines be recovered from Gamma_0, Gamma_1, and Gamma_2 alone, without separately supplying the empirical mean, and if not, what is the exact covariance-only equivalence class?

source_refs.claim: The foundational spectrum relates excitation and event intensities to complete second-order structure but does not isolate a finite set of binned covariance matrices.
source_refs.author: Alan G. Hawkes

source_refs.claim: Kernel recovery is formulated using first- and second-order statistics, with the baseline obtained after the mean intensity and integrated kernel are known.
source_refs.author: Emmanuel Bacry and Jean-François Muzy

source_refs.claim: Integrated second- and third-order cumulants consistently estimate the integrated kernel, showing how higher-order information can resolve algebraic ambiguity beyond simple covariance moments.
source_refs.author: Massil Achab, Emmanuel Bacry, Stéphane Gaïffas, Iacopo Mastromatteo, and Jean-François Muzy

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing characterization results keep mean intensity as a separate first-order input, while integrated-cumulant matching adds third-order information. The concrete vacancy is whether the diagonal jump contribution inside zero-lag bin covariance already encodes intensity under the acyclic common-decay restrictions. The obstacle is to separate that Poisson diagonal term from integrated excitation covariance without presuming A invertible; failure would have to be exhibited by two legal positive-baseline parameterizations with the same three covariance matrices.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either an explicit formula mapping (Gamma_0, Gamma_1, Gamma_2, Delta) to (lambda, beta, A, mu), or a complete family of distinct legal parameterizations with identical three covariance matrices.

writing_exemplar.why: Its separation of first- and second-order inputs provides the cleanest framing for asking whether binning folds the missing first-order information into Gamma_0.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: full first and second order statistics characterize Hawkes dynamics -> fixed-bin covariance retains a diagonal jump contribution -> determine whether that contribution makes the mean a redundant input

method_exemplars.technique: Factor the Bartlett spectrum into the Hawkes transfer function and the diagonal innovation-intensity matrix.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The covariance-only question asks whether a finite collection of inverse-Fourier bin integrals preserves enough of that factorization to recover the diagonal intensity.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate empirical integrated cumulants and fit their algebraic Hawkes identities by moment matching with a consistency argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: If Gamma_0 supplies the missing diagonal moment, an analogous plug-in moment map gives an estimator and a route to its joint limit law.

open_problems.open_problem: For an acyclic multivariate Hawkes process with edge-specific exponential decay rates, what finite number of fixed-bin covariance lags is necessary and sufficient to identify the labeled graph, amplitudes, decay rates, and baselines?

source_refs.claim: The multivariate binned MC-EM model permits separate edge amplitudes and decay rates and estimates them numerically, but supplies no finite-lag injectivity or minimal-lag theorem.
source_refs.author: Leigh Shlomovich, Edward A. K. Cohen, and Niall Adams

source_refs.claim: General kernel matrices are identifiable from the entire continuous covariance function, leaving open how much fixed-bin lag information suffices under finite-dimensional heterogeneous exponential structure.
source_refs.author: Emmanuel Bacry and Jean-François Muzy

source_refs.excerpt: A future retry would need partial observation, unknown generators, or a genuinely causal identification problem
The exact real information-order frontier, the real feasible atlas, finite-sample inference ... remain open.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The common-decay model yields a single matrix semigroup whose nilpotent logarithm can be inverted on im(A). Edge-specific decay destroys that closure: the lag sequence comes from a higher-dimensional realization with multiple poles, and repeated decay rates create collisions. Web searches found latent-time likelihood and full-spectrum estimators but no theorem giving the minimal finite lag order or the real observational-equivalence locus. The prior generator and LiNGAM proposals point to unknown-generator recovery and finite-information compatibility fibers as the needed machinery. The first proof step must change from a restricted logarithm of one transition to a minimal-realization or matrix-pencil analysis of a matrix-valued exponential sum.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-lag Hankel or matrix-pencil characterization giving generic and nongeneric injectivity conditions, an explicit recovery algorithm, and counterexamples at every smaller lag order or at pole-collision configurations.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames heterogeneous multivariate decay estimation in the exact binned-data regime and makes the computational-versus-identification distinction visible.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: real multivariate counts are aggregated -> different interactions may decay on different scales -> determine when finitely many observable lag moments separate those scales and directions

method_exemplars.technique: Use the analytic covariance transfer relation and uniqueness of its causal factor to connect observable second-order structure to the full kernel matrix.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It establishes that heterogeneous kernel parameters are encoded in second-order information before the stronger finite-lag compression is attempted.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate Hawkes dynamics from bin-count spectra and derive consistency and asymptotic normality under mixing.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A finite-lag matrix-pencil estimator uses the same dependent binned process and faces analogous pole-separation and limit-theory issues.

open_problems.open_problem: Can covariance lags beyond Gamma_2 provide a calibrated overidentification test of the common-decay acyclic exponential Hawkes model against heterogeneous decay, feedback cycles, and nonexponential kernels?

source_refs.claim: Approximate INAR and binned-likelihood procedures can be severely biased and variable under binned observation, motivating diagnostics that distinguish model failure from optimization error.
source_refs.author: Leigh Shlomovich, Edward A. K. Cohen, Niall Adams, and Lekha Patel
source_refs.venue: Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics

source_refs.claim: Integrated Hawkes cumulants are fitted through moment matching, providing a precedent for testing surplus algebraic Hawkes moment restrictions.
source_refs.author: Massil Achab, Emmanuel Bacry, Stéphane Gaïffas, Iacopo Mastromatteo, and Jean-François Muzy

source_refs.claim: Binned Hawkes counts admit mixing-based spectral limit theory, but the paper estimates a specified model rather than testing finite-lag semigroup restrictions implied by common decay and acyclicity.
source_refs.author: Felix Cheysson and Gabriel Lang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact recovery from Gamma_1 and Gamma_2 imposes checkable restrictions on Gamma_3 and later lags, whereas binned-Hawkes papers generally assess fit by likelihood, Whittle contrast, or time rescaling. The natural covariance residual is rank constrained and plugs in parameters obtained through a truncated image and matrix logarithm, so its null law is not an ordinary smooth GMM chi-square law near rank changes or weak edges. Targeted searches found no calibrated test of this particular fixed-bin semigroup restriction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A covariance-residual statistic based on Gamma_3 through Gamma_L with a basis-invariant HAC or multiplier-bootstrap null law and consistency against explicitly stated cyclic, heterogeneous-decay, and nonexponential alternatives.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates diagnostics from the practical fact that coarse binning can make plausible Hawkes estimators highly biased.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: binned timestamps are unavoidable -> common approximations can bias parameters -> use surplus covariance restrictions to falsify the assumed Hawkes mechanism

method_exemplars.technique: Construct empirical Hawkes moment arrays and compare them with algebraic model moments through a GMM-style objective and consistency proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed test is an overidentifying-restrictions version of Hawkes moment matching, with lag covariances replacing integrated cumulants.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate long-run covariance under temporal dependence and calibrate coordinatewise maxima by Gaussian multiplier bootstrap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A graph-wide specification diagnostic requires simultaneous control of many dependent covariance residuals.

open_problems.open_problem: What simultaneous confidence set for an acyclic Hawkes graph is honest across unknown rank, disconnected components, local-to-zero edges, and the zero-edge nonidentified stratum, and what adaptation price is unavoidable?

source_refs.excerpt: The continuum rank-and-strength interval ... and the sharp simultaneous excess remain the stated open-ended question.
at γ_H=0, set-valued output or abstention remains mandatory

open_problems.why_unsolved: The weak-factor proposal shows that pairwise Gaussian moduli can miss mixture-driven costs at rank boundaries, while BACKSHIFT shows why a set-valued answer or abstention is mandatory at a nonidentified boundary. In two-lag Hawkes recovery, both the image dimension and graph support change discontinuously, and beta is not identified at the zero-edge law. The first proof step must replace the fixed low-rank Gaussian experiment by a local experiment for dependent binned counts and determine whether mixtures over ranks, edge locations, and topological orders force a larger honesty cost than pairwise local alternatives. Fixed-margin delta-method inference from the preceding opportunity cannot answer this boundary question.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A data-only graph-and-parameter confidence set with uniform simultaneous coverage over an explicit union of rank and edge-strength strata, plus a matching minimax expected-diameter or inclusion-loss bound and either an attaining procedure or a sharp unavoidable adaptation factor.

writing_exemplar.why: Its formulation separates honesty over a union from performance on each constituent class, with Hawkes rank and graph support replacing smoothness classes.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: pointwise confidence sets can be small -> honesty over statistically indistinguishable strata couples their sizes -> adaptation may force excess diameter -> quantify that price at Hawkes rank and edge boundaries

method_exemplars.technique: Use ordered-modulus confidence-set arguments to compare stratumwise diameter under global honesty.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired object is one confidence set honest over a nonconvex union while its diameter is assessed separately on rank and edge-strength strata.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct inference for low-rank functionals without conditioning on a consistently pre-estimated rank, with explicit weak-rank regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Hawkes graph confidence must remain defined and valid when the covariance-lag image rank cannot be consistently selected first.

literature_map:
Hawkes (1971, Biometrika) gives the foundational spectral relation between excitation kernels, innovation intensities, and second-order point-process structure.
Bacry and Muzy (2016, IEEE TIT, arXiv:1401.0903) prove that full continuous-time first- and second-order statistics uniquely determine a stationary multivariate Hawkes kernel via Wiener–Hopf uniqueness.
Etesami et al. (2016, UAI) recover exponential Hawkes graphs from second-order moments, but use the full covariance spectrum and transforms of covariance density rather than two fixed-bin lag matrices.
Achab et al. (2017, ICML, arXiv:1607.06333) estimate the integrated influence matrix by matching second- and third-order cumulants, adding higher-order information rather than compressing to two lags.
Kirchner (2016, SPA, arXiv:1509.02007) establishes the Hawkes–INAR(infinity) connection; Kirchner (2017, Quantitative Finance, arXiv:1509.02017) turns bin counts into an INAR-based nonparametric estimator.
Cheysson and Lang (2022, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2003.04314) prove consistency and asymptotic normality of Whittle estimation from fixed-bin Hawkes counts while explicitly accounting for sampling aliasing.
Shlomovich et al. (2022, JCGS) show that naive binned likelihood and INAR approximations can be badly biased and propose latent-time BH-EM.
Shlomovich, Cohen, and Adams (2022, Statistics and Computing) extend latent-time MC-EM to multivariate binned Hawkes models with edge-specific amplitudes and decay rates.
Zhou and Papadogeorgou (2025, Bayesian Analysis, arXiv:2211.16552) prove distribution-level identifiability for aggregated Hawkes specifications and use latent-time Bayesian inference, a richer observable object than two covariances.
Xu, Farajtabar, and Zha (2016, ICML, arXiv:1602.04511) connect Hawkes impact-function support to Granger graphs and estimate it by sparse-group likelihood from event times.
Mark, Raskutti, and Willett (2019, IEEE TIT, arXiv:1802.04838) give sparse and low-rank learning bounds for discrete self-exciting autoregressive networks, not exact continuous-Hawkes bin integrals.
Wang et al. (2020, NeurIPS, arXiv:2006.07506) and Wang, Kolar, and Shojaie (2025, JASA, arXiv:2007.07448) provide Hawkes network uncertainty quantification from exact-time likelihood or integrated-history martingales.
Cai et al. (2024, TNNLS, arXiv:2105.10884) model graph-time topology in alarm sequences; Qiao et al. (2023, IJCAI, arXiv:2305.05986) explicitly frame low-resolution instantaneous effects as a causal-identification problem.
Across the targeted scan, no paper gives an exact mean-plus-two-bin-covariance inverse for singular acyclic common-decay Hawkes matrices or rank-adaptive simultaneous inference for that inverse.
The central tension is full-function, spectrum, or likelihood-based identifiability versus finite-lag algebraic sufficiency: existing work shows that richer observations contain the parameters but not that two fixed-bin lags retain them under the stated restrictions.
prior_proposal_map:
No directly Hawkes-specific prior proposal exists in the catalogue. The active eid_hawkes_fixedbin_dealias directory has no proposal core or reviews yet.
The closest direct predecessor is failed eid_survival_generator_commutator/v1: its README, gaps JSON, and pipeline JSONL were inspected; Stage -1.1 rejected known-generator BCH algebra and redirected work toward unknown-generator identification from partially observed transitions.
Accepted eid_robust_backshift_uniform_distance/v1 and downgraded panel_multispell_hankel_irregularity/v1 were mined through README, proto_core.json, writeup.tex, and review JSONs; their open boundaries concern conditioning margins, confidence-union contraction, and data-measurable simultaneous lag inference.
Downgraded stat_weak_factor_rank_adaptation/v2 was mined through README, core, writeup, pipeline, and reviews; its unresolved continuum rank/strength inversion and mixture-versus-pairwise obstruction support the honest-inference opportunity.
Downgraded stat_bdd_pointwise_first_bin_alias_frontier/v1 was mined through README, core, writeup, pipeline, and reviews; it supplies a within-bin null-direction/release-fiber template, though that more distant nonparametric partial-ID direction was filtered from the final ledger.
Downgraded eid_score_order_minimax_gap_v1/score_variance_gap_exponent was mined through README, core/writeup, reviews, three rejected cores, and two rejected proposal TeX archives; its minimax support-boundary direction was filtered as less direct than the retained inference gaps.
Accepted eid_lingam_direction_min_order_v1/truncated_cumulant_minimality was mined through README, core/writeup, reviews, rejected core, and three rejected TeX archives; its compatibility-variety machinery supports the heterogeneous-decay finite-information frontier.
Downgraded eid_lnsem_cumulant_id/v1 and eid_ganm_innovation_atomic_partition/v1 were also inspected but yielded no closer Hawkes opportunity.
